RSA key exchange: VPN for VPC uses Diffie-Hellman, not RSA, for key exchange. D. Post-shared key: There’s a pre-shared key (PSK) used for authentication, not “post-shared.” upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel

discussion: Selected Answer: BD IBM Cloud Transit Gateway is a high-performance private network backbone that simplifies and centralizes connectivity between VPCs, on-premises networks (via Direct Link), and Power Virtual Servers — all without routing traffic over the public internet. upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel

question: Monitoring data can be considered sensitive by some clients. How can a client configure IBM Cloud Monitoring so that sensitive monitoring data is not traveling across the public internet? A. Encrypt all monitoring data with a user-controlled key from Key Protect or Hyper Protect Crypto Services B. Configure the monitoring instance and monitoring agents to only use private endpoints C. Ensure that all resources being monitored are in the same region as the IBM Cloud monitoring instance D. Use only private endpoints to store monitoring data in IBM Cloud Object Storage
discussion: Selected Answer: B In IBM Cloud Monitoring (with Sysdig), monitoring data — such as metrics, logs, and system telemetry — can include sensitive operational information. To ensure this data does not traverse the public internet, clients can configure the service to use private endpoints. upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel

question: What describes a feature of IBM Cloud Transit Gateway when interconnecting multiple virtual private clouds (VPC)? A. Client designates which traffic remains within the private IBM Cloud backbone B. Provides private interconnectivity for on-premises workloads and the designated VPC C. Provides and defines connections between resources on the IBM Cloud network D. Provides a decentralized hub for better regional connectivity and load balancing
discussion: Selected Answer: C IBM Cloud Transit Gateway acts as a centralized network hub that allows clients to interconnect multiple IBM Cloud VPCs, on-premises networks (via Direct Link), and IBM Power Virtual Servers through IBM’s private backbone, rather than the public internet. upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel

question: Which encryption option allows clients to have control over the keys used to encrypt their block storage volumes, file shares, and custom images? A. Provider-managed encryption B. Client-managed encryption C. IBM-managed encryption D. Custom encryption
discussion: Selected Answer: B 🔒 Provider-managed encryption (default) IBM Cloud automatically manages the encryption keys. Clients have no control over key rotation or lifecycle. 🧩 Client-managed encryption (CME) → ✅ (Correct Answer) Clients can create and control their own encryption keys. Keys are stored and managed using: IBM Cloud Key Protect, or IBM Cloud Hyper Protect Crypto Services (for higher FIPS-certified protection). Clients can rotate, disable, or delete keys at their discretion. upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel

question: An organization wants to secure its exposed APIs running on IBM Cloud API Connect Reserved Instances using OAuth and OpenID. Which capabilities can help in this case? A. Authentication and authorization capabilities are offered by IBM API Connect itself B. IBM API Connect APIs must be secured by a third party as API Connect is responsible for managing the API life cycle only C. IBM API Connect is providing authentication, but authorization can be provided by IAM D. IBM API Connect creates user registries, but OAuth isn’t allowed in API Connect, and this can be done by a third-party provider
discussion: Selected Answer: A IBM API Connect provides built-in capabilities for both authentication and authorization using OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) standards. With these, you can: Protect APIs with OAuth 2.0 tokens. Integrate with OpenID Connect identity providers (like IBM Security Verify, Azure AD, etc.). Define and enforce security policies (client credentials, password, implicit, authorization code, etc.). Control access scopes and permissions directly in API Connect. upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel

question: An organization is using IBM Log Analysis to manage operating system logs, and platform logs in IBM Cloud. A developer discovered their Red Hat OpenShift on IBM Cloud instance is not being captured in the service. What could be a reason Log Analysis is missing the Red Hat OpenShift on IBM Cloud instance logs? A. The developer needs at least editor IAM role to the Log Analysis instance B. The administrator needs at least reader access to the Red Hat OpenShift instance C. The Red Hat OpenShift on IBM Cloud instance is running in a different region from the Log Analysis instance D. The logging agents were not created and deployed to this OpenShift instance
discussion: Selected Answer: D In IBM Cloud Log Analysis, logs are collected only when the proper logging agents are installed and configured on the resource or cluster you want to monitor — including Red Hat OpenShift on IBM Cloud. If the developer’s OpenShift cluster logs are missing, the most common cause is that the logging agents (such as the LogDNA or Activity Tracker agents) were not deployed to the cluster. upvoted 1 time Submit Cancel
